title: The Ideal Stocking Stuffer
description: Mine AdventCoins by finding the lowest number that, combined with a secret key, produces an MD5 hash starting with five (then six) zeroes.
writeup:
## The Puzzle

This is a simplified proof-of-work puzzle — the same basic idea behind Bitcoin mining. Given a secret key, find the smallest positive integer `n` such that `MD5(key + n)` starts with a required number of leading zeroes.

## Approach

There's no shortcut: MD5 is a one-way function, so the only option is brute-force iteration. For each candidate `n`, compute the hash and check the prefix:

```python
while True:
    digest = hashlib.md5(f"{key}{n}".encode()).hexdigest()
    if digest.startswith(prefix):
        return n
    n += 1
```

Part 1 requires five leading zeroes, part 2 requires six. The same function handles both — part 2 just takes roughly 16× longer on average since each additional zero digit makes the target 16× rarer.

## Note on Performance

Python's `hashlib.md5` calls into native C code, so it's reasonably fast even for the hundreds of thousands of iterations needed here. Running in Pyodide (WebAssembly) is slower than native, so expect a few seconds for part 2.

## Visualization

The animation samples every 500th candidate, showing the key, the number being tested, and its hash — until the five-zero solution flashes up.
